product_overview: DaviDev is a full-stack professional portfolio with a technical blog and a private CMS, built to demonstrate real engineering depth through public, auditable artifacts. It combines a bilingual public site, an article publishing system, and a case study page that documents how the product itself was built.
core_goals: Present the developer’s background, skills, experience, projects, and contact options in a way that quickly convinces technical evaluators and potential clients.
Provide a technical blog with searchable, filterable, well-rendered Markdown articles optimized for discovery and readability.
Enable secure administrative content management with JWT-based login, draft/publish editing, tagging, categorization, and versioned posts.
Expose the engineering process publicly through a case study page that makes methodology visible, not just outcomes.
Support bilingual public content (pt-BR and en) and light/dark theme preferences for broader accessibility and reach.
Enforce a hexagonal architecture with documented REST APIs, testable domain logic, and serverless-safe infrastructure patterns.

features.name: Public Portfolio Pages
features.description: Public-facing pages present the developer profile, background, skills, knowledge, experience, projects, and contact information for technical evaluators, recruiters, and potential clients.
user_flows: GET /pt-BR -> Receive 200 with localized home page content and navigation to Projects, Blog, Case Study, and Contact -> GET /pt-BR/projetos -> Receive 200 with highlighted project list and summaries -> GET /pt-BR/projetos/:slug -> Receive 200 with project problem, business outcome, technical decisions, and links

GET /en -> Receive 200 with English home page content and locale-aware navigation -> GET /en/about -> Receive 200 with biography and photo -> GET /en/contact -> Receive 200 with contact links and form
GET /api/v1/public/projects/:slug with nonexistent slug -> Receive 404 with a handled not-found response
GET /api/v1/public/contact with required locale and data missing -> Receive 400 with validation errors for the submitted fields

features.name: Bilingual Routing and Theme Support
features.description: The public site supports pt-BR and en locales with locale-aware URLs, persisted language preference, and light/dark/system theme switching that respects accessibility and system settings.
user_flows: GET /pt-BR/blog -> Receive 200 with Brazilian Portuguese article list and locale-specific labels -> Switch language to en via locale selector -> GET /en/blog -> Receive 200 with the same blog surface translated to English where available
GET /fr/blog -> Receive 302 or 307 redirect to the default locale path -> GET /pt-BR/blog -> Receive 200 with the default localized view
GET /en with system theme preference set to dark -> Receive 200 with dark theme styles and no flash of incorrect theme
POST /api/v1/preferences/theme with invalid theme value -> Receive 400 with a validation error response

features.name: Technical Blog Reading and Discovery
features.description: The blog lets readers browse published posts by category and tag, open articles by slug, and read sanitized Markdown with dates, metadata, and code highlighting.
user_flows: GET /pt-BR/blog -> Receive 200 with published posts ordered by publication date descending -> GET /pt-BR/blog?category=arquitetura&tag=fastify -> Receive 200 with filtered results reflected in the URL -> GET /pt-BR/blog/meu-artigo -> Receive 200 with rendered Markdown article, category, tags, publication date, and last update date when applicable
GET /en/blog/:slug for an article that does not exist in English -> Receive 200 with explicit unavailable-in-this-locale messaging or the locale-specific fallback behavior defined by content rules
GET /api/v1/public/posts/:slug with malicious Markdown content -> Receive 200 with sanitized HTML where scripts are not executed
GET /pt-BR/blog/:slug for a draft post -> Receive 404 or treated-not-found response, because unpublished content is never exposed publicly

features.name: Administrative Authentication and Session Management
features.description: The admin area is protected by JWT-based authentication with access and refresh tokens, supporting login, session renewal, and logout.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/auth/login with valid credentials -> Receive 200 with Access Token and Refresh Token -> POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with valid Refresh Token -> Receive 200 with a new Access Token
POST /api/v1/auth/login with invalid credentials -> Receive 401 with a generic authentication error and no user-existence disclosure
POST /api/v1/auth/logout with a valid Refresh Token -> Receive 204 or 200 confirming logout -> POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with the invalidated token -> Receive 401 requiring a new login
POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with expired or malformed token -> Receive 401 with an authentication error response

features.name: Administrative Content Management for Posts
features.description: The CMS allows the admin to list, create, edit, move to trash, restore, and permanently delete blog posts while preserving publishing rules and public visibility constraints.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/auth/login with valid credentials -> Receive tokens -> GET /api/v1/admin/posts with Access Token -> Receive 200 with draft, published, and trash states -> POST /api/v1/admin/posts with valid post data -> Receive 201 with the created draft or published post

GET /api/v1/admin/posts/:id with valid Access Token -> Receive 200 with post details -> PUT /api/v1/admin/posts/:id with updated content -> Receive 200 and updated timestamp -> POST /api/v1/admin/posts/:id/publish -> Receive 200 and make the post publicly visible

POST /api/v1/admin/posts/:id/trash with valid Access Token -> Receive 200 and move the post to trash -> GET /api/v1/admin/posts/trash -> Receive 200 with trashed posts -> POST /api/v1/admin/posts/:id/restore -> Receive 200 and restore the post to its previous state

POST /api/v1/admin/posts/:id/delete with valid Access Token -> Receive confirmation request -> POST /api/v1/admin/posts/:id/delete confirmed -> Receive 204 and permanently remove the record, its versions, and slug history
POST /api/v1/admin/posts with duplicate slug -> Receive 409 conflict or validation error indicating the slug is already in use

features.name: Markdown Editor and Live Preview
features.description: The CMS provides a Markdown editor with Editor, Preview, and Split modes, using the same rendering logic as the public article page for accurate authoring.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/admin/posts/:id/edit with valid Access Token -> Receive 200 with editor data and current Markdown content -> Open Preview mode -> Render the same article component used on the public site -> Save changes via PUT /api/v1/admin/posts/:id -> Receive 200 with the persisted content
GET /api/v1/admin/posts/:id/edit with invalid or missing token -> Receive 401 and deny access to the editor
PUT /api/v1/admin/posts/:id with missing required fields -> Receive 400 with field-level validation errors from shared schema
GET /api/v1/admin/posts/:id/preview with unsupported Markdown or unsafe HTML -> Receive sanitized preview output without script execution

features.name: Categories, Tags, and Post Organization
features.description: The admin can manage categories and tags used to organize content and power public blog filters.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/admin/categories with valid Access Token -> Receive 200 with category list -> POST /api/v1/admin/categories with a new name -> Receive 201 with the created category -> PUT /api/v1/admin/categories/:id -> Receive 200 with the updated category name

GET /api/v1/admin/tags with valid Access Token -> Receive 200 with tag list -> POST /api/v1/admin/tags with a new name -> Receive 201 with the created tag -> DELETE /api/v1/admin/tags/:id -> Receive 200 or 204 if the tag is not in use
DELETE /api/v1/admin/categories/:id when the category is attached to posts -> Receive 409 or explicit error indicating the category cannot be removed while in use
POST /api/v1/admin/posts with duplicate category or tag names in the payload -> Receive 400 or 409 with clear validation feedback

features.name: Post Versioning and Update Visibility
features.description: Published post changes that alter content text create a new version, and the public site shows when content was last updated.
user_flows: PUT /api/v1/admin/posts/:id with changed title, summary, or body -> Receive 200 and create a new PostVersion record -> GET /api/v1/public/posts/:slug -> Receive 200 with updated content and updated-at metadata
PUT /api/v1/admin/posts/:id with only metadata changes such as category, tags, cover image, slug, or status -> Receive 200 without creating a new version but with a refreshed last-updated timestamp
GET /api/v1/public/posts/:slug after the first publication and later content change -> Receive 200 with both publication date and last update date shown when they differ
PUT /api/v1/admin/posts/:id with no actual content change -> Receive 200 and no duplicate version record is created

features.name: Contact Submission and Notification
features.description: The contact surface lets visitors send messages to the developer, storing the message in the database first and then notifying by email, with captcha and rate limiting protection.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/contact with valid name, email, and message plus captcha token -> Receive 201 or 200 confirming submission -> Persist message in database -> Send transactional email notification -> Return success even if email delivery later fails and the database write succeeded
POST /api/v1/contact with database write failure -> Receive 500 or 503 and show that the submission failed because persistence is the source of truth
POST /api/v1/contact with missing or invalid captcha token -> Receive 400 or 403 with captcha validation failure
POST /api/v1/contact repeatedly within rate limit window -> Receive 429 when shared-store rate limiting threshold is exceeded

features.name: Architecture, Health, and API Documentation
features.description: The backend exposes a health check and Swagger/OpenAPI documentation while enforcing hexagonal boundaries, serverless-safe execution, and public API observability.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/health -> Receive 200 with healthy status and service metadata
GET /api/docs -> Receive 200 with Swagger UI and documented routes
GET /api/openapi.json -> Receive 200 with OpenAPI 3.0 schema for client generation
POST /api/v1/auth/login with malformed payload -> Receive 400 with documented validation errors consistent with the OpenAPI contract
